title: Quotient-completed tensor and maps into locally complete targets
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$ on $\mathcal C$ write $D(\mathcal O)$ for its unbounded derived module category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}$ for derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and $\otimes^L_{\mathcal O}$ for total derived tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I=(t_1,\ldots,t_s)$ a finitely generated ideal [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $B=\varprojlim_n\underline{R/I^n}$ on $\mathcal C$, and $B_n=\underline{R/I^n}$ with their canonical quotient maps [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $P,L\in D(B)$ be arbitrary. Set $P_n=P\otimes_B^LB_n$, $L_n=L\otimes_B^LB_n$ and
$$P\widehat\otimes L=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_{B_n/B}(P_n\otimes_{B_n}^LL_n),$$
where restriction is along $B\to B_n$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and the limit is the total derived limit of the strict quotient tower [def-weil-derived-limit]. There is a canonical isomorphism of strict derived towers
$$\bigl((P\otimes_B^LL)\otimes_B^LB_n\bigr)_n\cong(P_n\otimes_{B_n}^LL_n)_n,$$
identifying their quotient augmentations. Its total limit identifies $P\widehat\otimes L$, together with its map from $P\otimes_B^LL$, with the Koszul-derived $IB$-completion of $P\otimes_B^LL$.

For every $Q\in D(B)$ that is locally derived $IB$-complete, meaning $R\mathcal Hom_{B|_U}(B|_U[1/t],Q|_U)=0$ for every site object $U$ and $t\in(IB)(U)$, composition with that completion unit gives a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P\widehat\otimes L,Q)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes_B^LL,Q).$$
The tensor–Hom adjunction itself is not part of this statement.
For $R=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi_E)$ on a scheme's small pro-etale site this is the quotient-tower tensor of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]; targets in [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] satisfy the local completeness condition. No constructibility, separatedness or finite-Tor condition is imposed on $P,L$, and no equality between ordinary and completed tensor is asserted.

proof.text: Apply lem-sf-normalized-finite-tensor-comparison: for each finite coefficient sheaf, the restricted scalar total-tensor isomorphism sends (a*b) tensor (x tensor y) to (a tensor x) tensor (b tensor y). Conjugate the existing reductionStep by the comparisons at n+1 and n. The reductionStep generator formula and multiplicativity of the quotient map prove the required normalization on both scalar factors. For uniqueness, precompose any other normalized transition by the comparison at n+1. The generic total_extension_hom_ext helper of lem-pur-integral-tensor-transition-compatibility reduces equality to c tensor (x tensor y); the normalization with scalar factors c and 1 identifies both routes. Thus existence and uniqueness are proved without a new assumption or split-off theorem.

proof.text: For good representatives P,Q, apply kFlat_total_tensor_model to their total tensor H. Its degreewise site-flatness gives monoidal flatness by siteSheafTensorRightIso. The normalized quotient presentation therefore computes H. Set T to S.tensor followed by its quotient tower, beta to identity, V and b from the strict balancing comparison. The model isomorphism followed by the quotient comparison and the image of b is e; the strict comparison kappa is lem-sf-quotient-total-tensor-tower-comparison. Its generator equation supplies the required normalization.

proof.text: Set nu to the quotient completion unit whiskered by S.tensor. The beta-unit equation reduces to a functor mapping an identity. Use koszul_quotient_reflector: its unit-preserving isomorphism, inverted and whiskered by S.tensor, is gamma. The hom-inverse identity proves the Koszul unit equation. The same reflector supplies the Hom bijection into every complete target.

proof.text: In the integral category, take a good representative of K by the existing localization. Choose a prime greater than l and the principal coefficient datum. Conditions (ii) and (v) of roosIntrinsicCompletenessEquivalence turn local vanishing into invertibility of eta_K. Use lem-sf-integral-completion-unit-inverted and a categorical argument. If F(eta_M) and eta_K are invertible, precomposition with eta_M is bijective: a preimage of f is F(f) followed by eta_K inverse. For injectivity cancel F(eta_M) after applying F, then use naturality and cancel eta_K. Apply this to M equal to ordinary tensor; completedTensor is its completion by definition.

proof.text: A target in [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] satisfies [def-weil-derived-complete] by definition. The datum hypotheses required by [lem-pur-roos-intrinsic-completeness-equivalence] hold by [lem-a1-principal-koszul-strict-replacement]: the valuation ring is Noetherian and its quotients are finite and perfect with the stated two-term free resolutions. Conditions (i) and (ii) of the Roos/intrinsic equivalence therefore give precisely local derived $\varpi_EB$-completeness of the target. If an auxiliary prime distinct from $\ell$ is needed for that node's notation, take $3$ when $\ell=2$ and $2$ otherwise. Its statement requires no condition on the scheme. This establishes the last specialization without imposing a bound or a finite-Tor condition on $P,L$. The Lean proof of integralConstructible_locallyComplete first applies [lem-sf-derived-complete-legacy-comparison] to the completeness clause of sfIntegralConstructible. Choose an auxiliary prime p greater than l, and use the finite-field datum with base ZMod p, exponent one and its algebraic closure. The good-representative localization for IntegralOnSlice is essentially surjective, so choose a good representative P of K. Apply conditions (i) implies (ii) of [lem-pur-roos-intrinsic-completeness-equivalence], using the datum furnished by [lem-a1-principal-koszul-strict-replacement]. The bounds and constructibility of the reductions are not needed for this implication.
